newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Sweden's Persson criticises EU wage levels.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Persson criticises EU wage levels.

text.p: Swedish prime minister Goran Persson criticised on Tuesday the high wage levels in European Union institutions, saying they harmed the credibility of the 15-nation bloc.
"The salaries in these institutions are too high and the benefits are too big," Persson told reporters.
"And I think this is something which harms the credibility in the whole of the European Union."

Persson was responding to questions following a Swedish radio report that showed many Swedish EU officials took home far higher net salaries than Swedish parliamentarians or even the Swedish Prime minister.
But Persson, on an official visit to Luxembourg, said Sweden had not been particularly successful in convincing other EU countries to try to reduce the wage and benefit levels at EU institutions.
